name: Parallel filter chains for rhythmic pad motion
goal: Thicken cinematic pads with parallel processing: run dual filters in parallel (e.g. low-pass + band-pass) with independent rhythmic/LFO cutoff motion synced to tempo, stack overlapping bands that a gentle bus compressor tames, and EQ lows after the parallel stack—portable alternative to only insert-filtering a single path.

source.title: Make basic sounds interesting with parallel processing!

prerequisites: DAW or synth FX rack supporting parallel chains/buses; dual filters; tempo-syncable LFO or step/rhythm modulator; optional bus compressor

inputs.name: rhythm_bars
inputs.description: Length of synced rhythm shape in bars

outputs.name: parallel_filter_rack
outputs.description: Tempo-moving parallel filter stack on pads

constraints: Ground every step in the source YouTube-provided Show-transcript text; do not invent UI paths or numeric settings not stated there.
Original synthesis / signal-flow only — map brand UI to portable osc/filter/env/LFO/FX modules for Traveler-inspired or Web Audio hybrid; never rip presets, wavetables, or samples.
Prefer transferable parameter relationships over vendor-specific preset or bank names.
Not affiliated with the plugin/hardware vendors named in the source video; recreate with comparable modules.
Transcript builds on layered pads then parallel FilterFreak-style dual filters; recreate with stock dual-filter parallel racks—do not require that plugin.

steps.action: Start from layered pad material (body + harmonic spice + optional melodic layer). Route the group into a parallel FX rack rather than only serial inserts.
Create a chain with two filters in parallel mode (example: low-pass on filter 1, band-pass on filter 2) so each path emphasizes different bands simultaneously.
steps.expect: Two differently filtered images of the same pad

steps.action: Drive both cutoffs from a tempo-synced rhythm/LFO shape (example: 1-bar custom shape, BPM-synced). Let the two filters move separately so motion is stereo/spectral, not a single sweep.
steps.expect: Rhythmic spectral motion over each bar

steps.action: Expect overlapping bands to stack in level; follow with a compressor on the parallel bus to squash volume spikes from constructive overlap. Prefer fixing sources when possible; bus compress is a lazy safety.
EQ after the parallel filters to remove excess low end created by the stack. Optionally add further parallel chains (saturation, etc.) that may overlap bands—keep compressor/EQ as glue.
steps.expect: Clear low end; animated parallel pad

steps.action: Optional stereo trick from transcript: when a rhythm modulator supports stereo shapes, set phase/offset between L/R so upward ramps become opposing L/R motions for width.

verification: Bypass parallel rack → static pad; engage → rhythmic spectral motion
LP and BP (or chosen pair) are both audible in parallel
Bus compressor/EQ prevents boom/spikes when bands overlap
